description.p: Tincan is a lightweight SIP softphone for the Linux desktop: a compact window with a dialpad, quick answer and hang-up, and very little in the way.

It supports multiple SIP accounts, several simultaneous calls with hold, transfer, local conferencing and recording, contacts with presence, call history, SIP MESSAGE chat, desktop notifications and handling of sip:, tel: and callto: links.
Tincan is inspired by the MicroSIP softphone for Windows. It is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by MicroSIP.

ul.li: Pressing a dialpad key plays its DTMF tone locally; the caller does not hear it.
New setting "Play keypad tones" in Settings, Calls.

description.p: Packages for Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22.

ul.li: A .deb package for Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22.
The AppImage now runs on systems with glibc 2.39 or newer.
Qt 6.4 is the minimum supported Qt version.
Call recordings and the call database are readable only by their owner.
Caller names in desktop notifications are shown as text, never as markup.
Recordings never overwrite an earlier file.
A finished call can no longer hang up a new call that reused its id.
Recordings no longer capture the microphone while the call is muted.
The single-instance socket is always private to the user.
